title: Affineness of a fibrewise closed open with full generic fibre over a Dedekind base
statement: Let $B$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension at most one, put $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $p:X\to S$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $i:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] which is quasi-compact as a morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: the inverse image of every affine open of $X$ is quasi-compact. For $s\in S$ write $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $U_s=U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-residue-field]. Assume that $U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ as open subschemes, and that $|U_s|$ is closed in $|X_s|$ for every $s\in S$. Then $i$ is an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. No flatness, finite-type, quasi-compactness or separatedness hypothesis on $p$ or $X$ is imposed. Empty fibres and $U=X$ are allowed.

proof.text: Identify $U$ with its image open in $X$ using [def-weil-open-immersion]. Fix an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, let $\varphi:B\to A$ be its structural ring map, and write $Z=V\setminus U=V_A(I)$ for an ideal $I\subseteq A$, using the description of Zariski closed subsets in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes]. Put $M=\varphi(B\setminus\{0\})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding], $\operatorname{Spec}(M^{-1}A)$ maps onto precisely those primes of $A$ whose contraction to $B$ is zero. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] these are the points of the generic fibre in $V$. The full-generic-fibre hypothesis therefore says that no prime of $M^{-1}A$ contains all the elements $f/1$ with $f\in I$.

The opens $D(f/1)$ for $f\in I$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}(M^{-1}A)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](i) gives a finite expression $1=\sum_{j=1}^r(a_j/\varphi(s_j))(f_j/1)$, with $a_j\in A$, $f_j\in I$, and $0
e s_j\in B$. Put $d=\prod_js_j$ and $d_j=\prod_{k
e j}s_k$. Multiplying the equality by $d$ and using the equality relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $0
e t\in B$ with $\varphi(t)(\varphi(d)-\sum_ja_j\varphi(d_j)f_j)=0$ in $A$. Thus $b=td
e0$ and $\varphi(b)=\sum_j\varphi(t)a_j\varphi(d_j)f_j\in I$. Consequently $Z\subseteq V_A(\varphi(b))$ and $D_V(\varphi(b))\subseteq U$. Empty sums and the zero localized ring cause no problem: take $d=1$ and use the same equality relation.

proof.text: The closed subset $E=V_B(b)\subseteq S$ is finite and consists of closed points. Indeed $S$ is locally Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and the definition [pqf-def-locnoeth], and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](iii). Hence [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] writes $E$ as finitely many irreducible closed subsets. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes](2) each such subset is $V_B(\mathfrak m)$ for a prime containing $b$. Since $b\ne0$, this prime is nonzero. In a domain of dimension at most one a nonzero prime is maximal: a larger prime would give the chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak m\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ of length two. Thus $V_B(\mathfrak m)=\{\mathfrak m\}$, by part (1) of the same cited node. The chain length convention is [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. This proves both assertions about $E$.

source.place: Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components), with Algebra Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible) and the dimension bound.

proof.text:
Let $x\in Z$, put $s=p(x)\in E$, and set $T=S\setminus(E\setminus\{s\})$, an open neighbourhood of $s$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] the closed subset $|U_s|\subseteq|X_s|$ identifies with $U\cap p^{-1}(s)$. Since $s$ is closed in $S$, this is closed in $X$, and hence its intersection with $V$ is closed in $V$. Therefore
$$W=(V\cap p^{-1}(T))\setminus(U\cap p^{-1}(s))$$
is open in $X$ and contains $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose an affine open $W_x$ with $x\in W_x\subseteq W$.

On $W_x$ one has $U\cap W_x=D_{W_x}(\varphi(b)|_{W_x})$. To check this, a point of $W_x$ where $b$ vanishes lies over a point of $E\cap T=\{s\}$ and cannot belong to $U$, by the definition of $W$. At a point where $b$ does not vanish, the inclusion $D_V(\varphi(b))\subseteq U$ of step 2 applies. This proves equality of the underlying opens and therefore equality as open subschemes, by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme] makes this principal open affine, even if its defining element is a zero divisor or nilpotent. For $x\in U$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] instead gives an affine neighbourhood $W_x\subseteq U$, whose inverse image in $U$ is itself.

source.place: Tag 07ZT (lemma-complement-locally-principal-closed-subscheme), principal-open calculation; Schemes Tags 01I3 and 01IT.

proof.text: Perform this construction in affine charts covering $X$. The resulting affine opens $W_x$ cover $X$, and the inverse image of each under $i$ is affine by step 5. Apply [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] to this cover to conclude that $i$ is affine. The construction only used the Noetherian domain and dimension bound on $B$, the full generic fibre, and fibrewise closedness. It imposed no finiteness or flatness on the chart algebra $A$. If a boundary is empty, only the neighbourhoods inside $U$ are needed; an empty principal open is affine as well.
